passage: Come here, beta, and sit. You asked how I knew what to say to you last week, so I'll tell you. I'm Pooja. I was sixteen then, and there was a girl in my class called Vasudha. Whenever she walked into the room my whole body noticed. I didn't know what that pull meant. I only knew my family had a picture of my future, and I couldn't tell if this fit inside it. I didn't tell anyone for months, and I kept trying to name it and getting scared. Finally I told my cousin Reena, who only said, "You don't have to know today." I can still remember how my shoulders dropped. I took my time. I stayed honest with myself and I didn't rush to any label. That patience is what I'm giving you now.

qa.q: What was the name of the girl in Pooja's class?
What was Pooja feeling in those months, and how can you tell?
qa.a: Confused and worried. Pooja did not know what the pull meant, could not tell if it fit the family's picture of the future, and kept trying to name it and getting scared.

qa.q: What helped Pooja most, and what does it suggest a wise person might do?
qa.a: Telling cousin Reena, who said Pooja did not have to know today, helped. Talking to someone trusted and taking time worked better than rushing to a label.

qa.q: How might Reena have seen Pooja's confession?
qa.a: Reena probably wanted Pooja to feel safe rather than pushed, which is why Reena said Pooja didn't have to know that day.

grounding: Pooja felt a strong pull toward a classmate and was unsure what it meant or how it fit family expectations; Pooja took time and confided in someone trusted.

passage:
Dear Masi,
You said I can write to you about anything, so here goes, and please don't tell Mummy yet.
There's a boy in my class, Lokesh. We're partners in the chemistry project. I can't stop thinking about him. When he laughs, I feel warm all over. When he talks to other girls, I feel strange and sad.
I don't know what this is. Is it a crush? Is it just friendship? And also, he's from a different community, and you know how Papa talks about "our kind." I feel guilty even for thinking about him.
I'm not going to do anything yet. I don't even know what I'd do. I just needed to tell someone I trust.
Can you call me on Sunday? You're the only one who won't panic.
Your confused niece,
Sonali

qa.q: Which project are Sonali and Lokesh partners in?
How is Sonali feeling about Lokesh?
qa.a: She feels a strong pull toward him, warm when he laughs, but confused and guilty because of her family's expectations.

qa.q: What is Sonali doing that is wise?
qa.a: She is taking her time, not rushing to label the feeling or act on it, and talking to a trusted adult, her Masi.

qa.q: How might Masi respond when she reads the letter?
qa.a: Masi will probably feel touched to be trusted and want to reassure Sonali calmly, since Sonali says Masi won't panic.

grounding: A teen feels a strong pull toward a classmate, is unsure what it means or whether it fits family expectations, and turns to a trusted aunt.

passage:
You asked me what the hardest thing about Class 11 was? Honestly, it wasn't exams. I'm Shreya, and it was Ritu.
Ritu's my best friend. We've done everything together since we were ten. But last year something shifted. When she held my hand crossing the road, my heart went crazy. When she talked about a boy she liked, I felt sick and couldn't explain why.
I didn't know what it meant. Was it just close friendship? Something more? And my family has very fixed ideas about who I'll marry one day, so even thinking the question felt dangerous.
I didn't say anything to Ritu. I didn't try to name it. I went to the school counsellor, who said, "You don't need an answer this week. Feelings can take time to understand."
That helped so much. I'm still figuring it out, slowly. And Ritu's still my best friend.

qa.q: What did the school counsellor say to Shreya?
qa.a: "You don't need an answer this week. Feelings can take time to understand."

qa.q: How did Shreya feel when Ritu talked about a boy she liked?
qa.a: Shreya felt sick and confused, unable to explain the feeling, which added to the uncertainty.

qa.q: Which choice helped Shreya, and why?
qa.a: Talking to the school counsellor without rushing to a label gave Shreya permission to take time.

qa.q: How might Ritu see their friendship right now?
qa.a: Ritu probably sees it as the same close friendship as always, since Shreya has not told her about the changing feelings.

grounding: A teen feels a strong, confusing pull toward a friend, takes time, and talks to a trusted counsellor without rushing to a label.
